geeklist.title: Virtual Flea Market for Delivery to BGG.Spring 2023
geeklist.description:
[size=24][b]THIS EVENT IS OVER [/b] [/size]
Hello All! It's time for the the BGG.Spring 2023 Virtual Flea Market! I am you host for this year as Seppo will not be attending so hopefully it will be smooth sailing.
If you are new to the VFM or unsure of something please, please read the general information posted as Item number 1 in this geek list. It should hopefully answer any questions and if not comment on the item and people will gladly help.
[b]Main information[/b] Where: Innovation Ballroom When: Friday, May 26th Sellers: 7pm -7:50 [b]ALL SELLERS MUST BE INSIDE NO LATER THAN 7:50pm.[/b] Buyers: 8pm - 9pm
[u][size=18][b]TABLE SIGNUP CLOSED[/b][/size][/u] - You can still sell and list games but you will not get any allocation towards a table during the meetup which means if you don't have a table please schedule to meet up with people outside the VFM!
Table assignments! [imageid=7524888 original]
[geeklist=313509]BGG Spring 2023 VFM Request List[/geeklist] [url=https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=313443]BGG VFM 2023 sortable list[/url] Provided by Dave Rathbun thank you!
[b]Note[/b]: the sortable list does make use of the MARK SOLD Button Below your item's picture, use that over putting sold in the text it is more reliable.
[b]REMEMBER DO NOT DELETE YOUR LISTINGS[/b]

[q="drathbun"][q="ath3ist"]Is there a (good) reason so many games on this list have sold, but not been marked as sold using the geeklist feature?[/q] It's a newer GeekList feature, so some folks might not be aware of how it works.[/q] Folks, as a side note, there are three ways that my search index will move something from "available" to "sold" (and I think there are other search index tools that operate in a similar way).
The most reliable way to mark something sold is to use the mentioned "Mark Sold" button that now appears on your Geek List items. This has several advantages. First, it's a specific action that has exactly one meaning, which from a programmer perspective is nice. 🙂 The next (and also mostly reliable) if you don't choose that option is to add the tag [c]+sold+[/c] to the text of your listing (not in a comment). This is not likely to happen by accident, so the odds of your listing getting marked sold incorrectly are low. Finally, if you have the bare world "sold" anywhere in your listing the index will assume that means it's sold. At one point there was a problem (bug) where the letters s-o-l-d within another word (like soldier) would also trigger your item to be marked as sold, but that was corrected some time back.
Based on traffic, there are quite a few folks using my index / search tool so I thought I would share this quick update. I think if sellers can take one of the above steps to mark their items as sold it helps buyers understand what is still available. Thanks!

[q="drathbun"][q="ath3ist"]Is there a (good) reason so many games on this list have sold, but not been marked as sold using the geeklist feature?[/q] It's a newer GeekList feature, so some folks might not be aware of how it works.[/q] My guess for some of them - I have them listed on the geekmarket so I actually have to go into the geekmarket and mark it sold there so I don't have duplicate entries. Hi folks, I am happy to announce a new feature for the Sundered Realm hosted list index - you can now track / filter items by BGG username. I think this will be especially useful for those of you that are listing dozens (if not hundreds) of items as it makes it easier to see exactly what you're doing. For example, Michelle English (aka Cheelara1) has well over 100 games listed. Well, Michelle (and everyone else) you can now see just your games by adding [c]u=Cheelara1[/c] (insert your own username there) to the URL.
For example: https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=313443&u=Cheelara1&mode=9&sort=0
That will on a single list allow Michelle to see what she has listed and sold. The "User Sort" link is still active but it's rather pointless as everything on the list will be for one single user (seller) so it won't do anything. The preferred method of sorting should be "Game Sort" and that's what is in the link above.
My link would be: https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=313443&u=drathbun&mode=9&sort=0
If you encounter any errors or issues with this new feature, please let me know via GM and I'll sort them out.

Hope you all had a good Spring Con!

[q="steentx"]Is there any sort of policy or guidance on how to handle buyers who ghost you after agreeing to purchase a game? ... How do others handle this issue?[/q] It's unfortunate. I have had this happen in the past as well. I tend to send a follow-up Geek Mail and if there's no response I let it go. Other issues that I've had in the past are games with missing components, games that were listed as "like new" that I would have graded differently, or the opposite side - sellers that didn't show up to sell. 🙂 Last year I and another person both bought Memoir 44 stuff from the same seller. When I got home, I had extras of some stuff, and was missing some other components. I contacted the other buyer with my list, and sure enough, everything I was missing went home with him (and vice versa). Between the two of us we resolved it by mailing stuff. From that point forward I do my best to check / inventory used (opened) games at the convention so I have time to resolve issues before everyone leaves.
My overall experience with the VFMs in general has been super positive. I try to not let the occasional issue detract from that.

Overall my experience has been overwhelmingly positive. I really enjoy participating in both the VFM and Bazaar. I understand there is some risk. In fact last year at the bazaar I got a grail game (at least for me) and I was so excited I didn't get the seller's name, nor did I check contents until I got home. Sure enough it was missing about 1/4 of the components. I try to learn each time, and that is why I was asking to see what others do in this case. It sounds like I should let the VFM buyers know that if they don't pre-pay, or pickup the game at VFM, I will sell it at the Bazaar.
One of the cool things that someone at the VFM taught me a few years back was how to use MS Word to print on post-it notes so that not only do I know who is buying the game, but it also has my info for them in case they have an issue after the sale.

item.body:
[b][size=24]BASIC INFORMATION AND RULES[/size][/b]
[b][size=18]Event Tickets[/size][/b]
There is no longer a TTE Seller ticket requirement for this event. Instead you will be required to fill out my google sheet linked in the header (when it's finished) to reserve a table at the event. There are 60 tables for the event so i will be limiting it to 60 sellers. You will be allowed one helper that will be specified in the signup form.
Buyers can claim at ticket on TTE to help them remember the place and time but it is not required.
[b]General[/b]
The primary purpose of the Virtual Flea Market is to arrange the selling of games before arrival at the convention. If you have items that you'd like to sell at BGG.Spring, add a geeklist item including what you wish to sell. Please include the condition of your item and the price or terms you'd like to sell for. Then you will simply swap the game for payment at the meetup with the buyer.
The in person event is not a sales event simply an exchange of deals made on this geeklist beforehand. Please do not try and set up a sales table (had a person do that in November once), if you are looking to set up an in person sales table you are looking for the awesome BGG Bazaar (insert bgg link once it's up).
[b]Guidelines[/b]
How you sell your items is up to you! Fixed Price, Auction, Dutch Auction, it doesn't matter. Everyone is on their own - no one will be monitoring your items but you. If you are running an auction, please be sure to define how that auction is going to run, particularly how/when it is going to end.
Please be polite. Some buyers will make potentially lowball offers. Some sellers won't be interested in making deals. Please be respectful in your interactions.
Please [b]do not delete items [/b]once they are added to the list. If an item is no longer available, please edit your listing to indicate it is not available.
[b]Delivery Meetup[/b]
As in the past, we have a reserved time and space at BGG.Con Spring to make the swaps in the Innovation Ballroom on friday May 26th.
Sellers will be allowed to enter starting at 7pm in order to setup. Current plan if for sellers to enter from Innovation D. Sellers will not be admitted after 7:50. Sellers will be required to have signed up on the google sheet it is likely to still be limited to 60 sellers. If you are unable to obtain a seller's table, you must make other arrangements for swapping your games. If you are not going to be able to be at the swap, you need to note this in the item description. By participating in the VFM list as a seller and obtaining a seller's table you are agreeing to arrive early to set up. You may bring one helper with you to help out at your table (information provided during signup). Sellers are expected to remain at their table until all items are sold. Based on 2022 numbers, there should be enough seller's tickets for anyone that sells more than 10 items. If you sell fewer than 10 items, please allow those who are selling more items to have first opportunity for seller's tickets. You and/or your helper are expected to be at your table for the entire duration of the VFM until you do not have anything left to sell.
Buyers are free to line up during this setup time but are not permitted inside yet. You can get a buyers ticket but these to help you plan your day and are not required. If you both buy and sell, you will need someone else to pick up your purchases or make other arrangements (Sellers again someone must be at your table during the entirety of the VFM). Buyers will be able to enter from 8 PM.
[u][size=18][b]PLEASE BE PROMPT![/b][/size][/u] as both a Buyer and as a Seller no one wants to be stuck waiting around until 8:59 with 1 game left to trade or a buyer stuck waiting for a no show seller because you didn't want to leave your game early.
You are, of course, welcome to arrange other times/methods for your swaps on an individual basis (but see the note about an early meetup below).
Team Geek will be present overseeing the meetup. It is expected that all participants will cooperate fully with Team Geek.
[b]Delivery Meetup Room Plan[/b]
In order to facilitate the meetup, tables will be assigned to sellers. Each seller with a seller's ticket will receive one table. There will be no sharing of tables. Prior to the convention, the room plan will be posted in this header. Tables will be arranged in alphabetical order by user name. If you get a seller ticket that does not clearly connect to your user name, please let me know. Tables will be labelled at the time of the meetup.
[b]Unsold Game Filter Tools[/b]
What is the sortable list? It's basically a dynamically updating listing of this geek list that lets you sort and filter rather than scroll through listings one by one. This way you can sort on a user, or on a letter, or look for a specific game.
Our list this year was provided by:
[user=drathbun][/user]
Thank you so much!
You can find it here and in the header: [url=https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=313443]BGG VFM 2023 sortable list[/url]
In order for your games to better show up on this list the way you want to please follow the best practices below.
[b]Listing best practices[/b]
These are some best practices for listing your items in the VFM they help with the listing tools and are just great ways to have people understand your listing. These will be updated with any tool specific requirements.
1. When your item sells, please use your Mark sold button directly below the picture of your game.
2. If your item is an auction, please include the word "Auction" someplace.
4. If you wish to remove an item from the summary list, add +remove+ in the game's entry. This tag takes precedence over everything else.
5. If you are selling an item that needs an alternate name in the summary list, please place this code in your item someplace: "+altname+ Whatever You'd Like To Call Your Item -altname-"
6. [b]Please don't delete sold items!! [/b]Just leave them on the list. Thank you!
7. Please do not mark items as SOLD if they are not actually SOLD
[b]Request List[/b]
If there is something you are looking for add it to the [geeklist=313509]BGG VFM 2023 Request List[/geeklist].
[b]Processing Payments[/b]
Per BGG Guidelines, it is the seller's responsibility to process final sales through the BGG Marketplace. This may be facilitated by use of the sold button below each item's picture. Some people like to do a single lump sum payment for everything or for items where the buyer did not respond to the listing. In the past I have used a listing under Outside the Scope of BGG for this simply add the item on the geekmarket for the amount you need and mark it sold.
[b]Early Meetup[/b]
In the past, some of the participants in the Fall VFM have tried to set up an early meetup on the night before the official start of the convention. This has been discouraged for several years now. While individuals getting together to make trades is certainly appropriate, please do not schedule a large-scale early meetup before the start of the convention.
[b]Please do add your items![/b] The more items, the more interest!
[b]Please do not delete items once added.[/b] If an item is no longer available, please edit it to reflect that, but leave it in place. You can add +remove+ to the entry to keep it off the summary list.
[b]Additional tips for sellers and buyers:[/b]
Sellers:
1. Create a spreadsheet with the games your selling. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Buyer Name, Buyer BGG Name, Comments, etc. If you're paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you.
2. Send out geek mails and confirm with the game sale with people who have bought games from you. Sometimes people miss responses to game transactions. Run your sales through BGG Marketplace either as a lot or individually so BGG can get their cut. It's only fair.
3. Have a full-length, printed sheet with your BGG User Name, Name, and Avatar/Logo on it for people to find you more easily.
4. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle your table.
5. Get there right at 7:00 pm to set up your games and table.
6. You must attend the whole hour or until all your games being sold are picked up by Buyers.
7. Team up with a friend (or a few friends) if you are both Buying and Selling games. You cannot be both a Buyer and Seller at the VFM event.
8. Removable Sticky notes on the game with the name of the Buyer picking up your games would be helpful.
9. Please get your money out of the envelopes and deposit the empty envelopes in the trash. Please do not leave it for staff to clean up!
10. Remember it's the most wonderful game time of the year! Be kind, courteous, and try to help others out as possible. This event is super fun!
Buyers:
1. Create a spreadsheet with the games you're buying. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Seller Name, Seller BGG Name, Comments, etc. If you're paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you.
2. Buy plain envelopes. Write down the name of each game you're buying and the BGG name of the Seller. Provide exact change. Put your name on your envelopes so it's easily identified as paid by sellers or in case it gets lost.
3. Get there around 7:45 pm and wait in line to get in. Buyers can't go in until 8:00 pm.
4. Bring plenty of bags to haul off your 'new' games. You may not be able to use the luggage carts.
5. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle or highlight the tables you need to visit.
6. Remember it's the most wonderful game time of the year! Be kind, courteous, and try to help others out as possible. This event is super fun!
There is a Virtual Flea Market microbadge Microbadge: BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market fan Get one and show your support for the VFM!
Still have questions/comments/concerns? Please comment on this item and people will be glad to help.
(if you want to help answer questions subscribe to this item)

item.body:
Item: Terraforming Mars Player Mat Overlay (Set of 5) Condition: Like New Price: $40
Description I don't really think I want to sell these, thus the higher price. I have 5 assembled acrylic player mat overlays from Board Game Boost (as pictured) for my Terraforming Mars game. I have since purchased the "Big Box" and have the dual layer cardboard trays, but honestly I still prefer these. If I could figure out a way to store them in my big box without altering the insert I would not even be considering this. There are two versions of this product. One is just an overlay, and the second is the same overlay but with a backing board so your TM play mat is completely enclosed in acrylic. That's the version I have, and they are awesome. They look like sparkly jewels on the game table. :)
But if you think you want them more than I do, I would sell the set of five for $40, already assembled, and including the player mats. For the record the trays with the backer board sell new for $10.99 (plus shipping) so you're not saving that much by buying at this price, but there is a bit of a discount.

Bardagi: The Claim for Gold is a card-driven, area management, adventure board game for 2-5 players, played in a number of rounds and each round is divided into 4 turn phases. Each player controls a group of Vikings; a Berserkur (your warrior), a Godi (your priest), a Kaupmadur (your merchant) and Knerrir (your Viking ship). These units are used to claim and overtake areas from the Barbarian tribes currently occupying the land. Players start at their home town and during the game, players overtake the areas surrounding their town to gain resources. Players gain resources each round, according to the areas owned, and with these resources they can reload the units, that are needed to overtake other areas, buy upgrades to improve their buildings, buy runes or trade resources in for gold. The aim of the game is to collect the most glory points within the given rounds to be declare the winner at game end.

item.comment: Can I add this to my pile for free?

Given how much you've bought from me, I'll sell it to you for $1 in cash or $5 in trade, your choice.
[i](spins invisible handlebar mustache)[/i]
I'm confused. I believe I've purchased over $40 from you, so per your description, I think I meet the requirements to add it for free?? Am I missing something? I'm sorry if I misunderstood

The (FREE) option was added yesterday as a sweetener to move product that wasn't moving. So it qualifies for any purchases moving forward.
However, because you're a good customer, I'm offering to sell it to you for $1. I'm not doing that to be a jerk, so much as so that it helps me generate a value to put in to the "Mark Sold" button, because it doesn't allow $0 as an option. So I'm offering to sell it to you for the smallest price possible that will generate a commission for the website. For anyone else buying in the future, I'll mark the final costs to make the totals work out correctly so that the marketplace gets its commission.
The trade option I put there on the off-chance you would rather do that, and I apologize if you took offense.
Ok 👍🏻 thank you for the clarification. That makes sense and I understand! I will buy for $1. And thank you!

Influentia is a card game based on classic trick-taking card games. In each trick, players play one of their Resource Cards. The winner of the trick may choose one of the City Cards from among those available or the Resource Card that was just played by another player. The other players keep the cards they played as these will allow them to activate a variety of effects once they have two identical Symbols. After three rounds, the player who has won the most victory points wins the game.

The players are a united faction of agents whose mission is to destroy the forces of the machine while hacking the network to take down the satellite before it’s too late.
In this fast-paced, action-packed, highly replayable cooperative game, 1-4 players make meaningful strategic choices that determine the fate of the world. Players work together to equip their agents, activate zone abilities, and combat the forces of Dominus while collecting intel to crack the code for deactivating the rogue satellite putting a stop to his plan. Once hacked, Dominus is forced to land on Earth and transform into a giant battle robot to face humanity the final showdown. This must all be done before Dominus overruns the world sending it into a chaotic terror and disarray thereby allowing his forces to subjugate and eradicate mankind.

item.body:
[size=18][b]Ginormous Heroscape Collection - $TBD[/b][/size]
This may not be the place to sell this, but I figured I'd float it in case there's interest. I essentially have at least three of pretty much everything ever made regarding terrain sets and figures that can be drafted in squads, and one of every unique figure. All of the cards have been kept in a CD binder, so they're in really great shape, and the figures are sorted into Plano bins.
The boxes are gone except two base set boxes, one Elite Onyx Viper base set box, two Marro base set boxes, three Battle for the Underdark base set boxes, and three Wall & Towers building pack boxes. I also have an assortment of sealed figure packs.
This is probably a 4-figure deal, so if anyone is seriously interested, shoot me a PM.

A fun programming game where players simultaneously select five action cards to be performed from the nine actions available and lay them down in order they are to be played. The turn is then resolved one card at a time. The actions allow players to place plank foundations, place planks, move their pawns, cancel other players' actions, or remove planks or foundation stones. As can be expected for a design with simultaneous action selection, the game is rather chaotic, and hilarious.

Open, excellent condition.

How about some nice aftershave from 1949? Or maybe you're looking for a fancy fly swatter from 2014? You just found a magical store that has all of these products and more! All it takes is a good eye and a fast hand, and these bargains can be yours!
Shop 'N Time is a real-time, app-assisted card game with simple rules. In the basic game mode, "Price Target", each player is given the same budget, then dealt a hand of seven cards. You pick one to purchase, pass the rest, possibly pick another, then pass, etc., and you keep going until you have at least three cards but think the price of those items is still within your budget. Once everyone passes, each player scans the items they've purchased to see who's come closest to spending the budget without going over.

Battle rages on between orcs and knights. Purple and Orange form a chaotic melee and no-one knows which side will win this battle. Mage towers scattered on the battlefield are strategic objectives, and it soon appears that whomever controls the most towers will reap the seeds of victory.
Players place tiles to form majorities of their army on the corners of towers: when all 4 corners are resolved, the player with the majority of corners seizes control of the tower.

Hi Kristine! Welcome!! Is this your first time to a bgg con or just to the vfm? Either way, we're super happy you are joining us! What I have done in the past is to put exact cash in an envelope with each seller's name on it and what I'm buying from them. Then I put them in alphabetical order and go through the room at pickup time and exchange envelopes for games. Nowadays some folks are also doing PayPal, Venmo, Cashapp, Zelle and so forth instead of handling cash. A few are going ahead and paying in advance so all they have to do is pick up their games, but plenty of others wait to do it in person, and there's still plenty of folks that do cash. It is totally up to you. I will send you a geekmail with my cell number so please write me back or feel free to text if you have any questions. Thanks again!

The following description is from [url]https://www.imagineeringstore.com/work-farce/[/url]
The game for the Great Resignation!
Congratulations, you quit! Since you've got plenty of time on your hands, why not play a game to help you figure out what's next? Tired of being a doctor or lawyer? Maybe you're better suited to be a donut hole maker or a pet food taster, a pirate or a telephone psychic. Work Farce will help you decide without all those time-consuming career tests and over-priced counselors. With Work Farce, all you have to do is answer insightful and insane multiple-choice questions to find your true calling.
Play Work Farce with quitters, new grads, post grads, the gainfully unemployed, and the painfully over-employed for hours of unpaid crazy career fun.

item.comment: How is the game play? Loved the books, enjoyed the TV series, wondering how well it translates to a board game. Doors and Corners...I remember that phrase from the books. The cop was talking about where you always need to check for trouble, doors and corners. 🙂

It's a very interesting take! The game play is very similar to a COIN (counter-insurgency) game, where you're trying to gain and keep influence and control over areas on the board, and interesting card-play and events. Think Twilight Struggle meets El Grande. You control a faction (UN, Mars, OPA, or Protogen), that each have unique abilities, and use action points to gain influence over the board though cubes and fleets. The main game is very playable on its own, but shines with the doors and corners expansion, which adds new technologies specific to each faction, extra cards, and a protomolecule that can destroy entire locations. It plays really quickly too.
I loved the series too, and the visuals from the show certainly help get into the spirit. My group didn't really care about the subject matter, so while we had a great game, I'm not getting it to the table.
Thanks for the info...I will keep an eye on the listing but it's more than I am willing to spend on it right now. Good luck with the sale!

SOLD for 125 to [user=xpiredsodapop][/user]
+altname+ Blokus Giant -altname-
[-]This is a copy of the GIANT Blokus they made years and years ago. The listed box dimensions per BGG are about two feet long by about two feet wide. It's BIG.
In truth, I have no idea what to list as the price because there's no sales history for this on the geek, or on ebay. I'm going to ask $125, because that's half the price that CamelCamelCamel suggests it went for the last time it was available new. I'm sure someone can correct me on that.
The type of box it's in means it's going to have wear; calling it a box is pretty generous. But the contents inside are just super, like it stepped out from a time machine.[/-]
item.comment:
[-]This could be fun do you have pictures of Giant Blokus? [/-]
[-]Edit: We also could have yard games and larger games in a section of the con. I'll think about $125. 🙂[/-] Was on the fence. Someone bought this. Congrats!
I can certainly get some. But what is your expected price range? I know you're collecting for a con prize table, and this feels like it's out of the price range of your stated mission.

Meanwhile, until I get back home, here's a link to someone else's picture to give you a sense of box size:
https://i.ytimg.com/vi/RQ150ioEe5A/maxresdefault.jpg
That's some serious box size-age!
I’m gonna need a bigger Kallax
[q="Zafin"]We also could have yard games and larger games in a section of the con. I'll think about $125. 🙂 [/q] No worries. Let me know what you decide.

No need to think, I'll take it for $125. Been looking for this for years... years after I saw it on Starlit Citadel years ago. Used to love watching their videos! I know Board Games with Scott did a quick segment on it too! 🙂

SOLD. Keep in mind if you're buying quite a few things at the VFM, this thing is its own trip. It's got a handle, but given the box design and the weight, you still want to support it with two hands. So expect to come in and out twice.

item.body:
$100
I have a copy of the Legendary Pledge of the original KS for Dead Reckoning. It is the one that was 109+shipping (which came to 135.81 after tax & shipping). AEG put the MSRP price at 190. In the second KS, this material would be slightly more expensive.
I really like the game. But with owning so many games and my main game group working our way through Frosthaven, it isn't going to hit the table in the next couple of years - so I'm OK with selling it. It's been played twice. Both ships have been assembled. The Saga 1: Deep Legends expansion is still in shrink.
That said, I'm also happy keeping it. I think it's aggressively priced given its unavailability. I'm not likely to haggle.

item.body:
Item: Colosseum (Days of Wonder edition as pictured, not the TMG reprint) Condition: NIS Price: $150
Description Yes, it's expensive. But in my opinion this is the premier edition of this game to own. As mentioned above, this is the Days of Wonder edition (pictured) and not the Tasty Minstrel Games reprint. If you have never played this game, it's quite interesting! You are putting on a show in the ancient Roman Colosseum. For each show you acquire actors, props, and a script. You put on one show a round, and you score points based on how well your show goes (did you have a complete cast, did you have enough people attending, were you able to entice a senator to view your performance). The money you make is then put into your next show. In one extremely interesting twist, you do not incrementally score during the game! Instead, only the best show score counts to determine the winner! It's entirely possible that you peak in a middle round and decline after that, leaving you at the mercy of the whims of the theater-going public as to whether they liked other shows better than yours...
I purchased it for $150 (yes, my asking price) on eBay over a year ago. (Actual cost to me was $170+ after tax and shipping.) I have since purchased an opened copy that is in pristine condition, so maybe there is a collector out there that would like to move this beauty from my collection to theirs! Price is firm. Willing to look at trades but only for things that I think I can reasonably flip for the same approximate value.

Item: Legend of the Five Rings Fate Coins Condition: New Price: $3

Description I could not find a listing for these anywhere on BGG, so I am going by what I found on eBay. These are apparently "Fate Coins" for the Legends of the Five Rings game. Not even sure which L5R game, as there are several. The coins are silver toned and have a decent amount of weight to them. They would probably work for any other game that could use a flower motif on a coin. There are no denominations; the flower you see in the image I attached is on both sides of the coin. Each coin is about the size of an American nickel (or even a Canadian nickel, which is much cooler because it has a beaver on it).
Anyway, I have seven bags of seven coins (as I was travelling to St Ives) and I'll sell them for $3 a bag or if you want all of them (I actually have eight but it didn't fit the quote I was going for) they'll be $15.

[q="dat008"]Interested, does it come with the promo cards attached?[/q] Common Ground Games (local to DFW area) has (or had) the deluxe Earth with the promo cards and wooden dirt tokens. I think they were $65 new.

James, sorry for the mix-up, would you be willing to let it go for $35 since it is the retail version? I understand if you want to give it more time.
Dave, do you know what are the major differences between the deluxe copy and retail? Also, what are in the promo cards?

Here's what I understand: Deluxe copy has wooden tokens that replace the "1" soil tokens and comes with a calendar of promo cards. There is one card for each month; you pick one at random (or as one person suggested to me, take the one for the month that you're playing the game) and place it next to the shared fauna goals. It affects everyone in the game in the same way. Something to mix it up a little bit.

Thanks for interest. I will hold for a bit and maybe play it a bit more if it doesn't go for my asking. I like the game quite a bit it just wasn't a have to own for me.
Thanks!

item.body:
Item: Firefly The Game B&N Exclusive Edition Condition: NIS Price: $40
Description This is ten bucks off the retail price for the B&N Exclusive edition of Firefly. What makes it exclusive, you ask? Great question, he answers! 🙂 It comes with the Artful Dodger ship (which used to sell for at least a Benjamin before it was reprinted) as that's shown right on the back cover. [q]The Artful Dodger starts with a faster drive core and trades in some Cargo Space for bigger Crew Quarters, making it a good ship for misbehaving in!
The Artful Dodger expansion includes everything you need to ship out in the Artful Dodger, including 1 Firefly Playing Piece (Turquoise), 1 Custom Dice, 1 Artful Dodger Ship Card and 1 Dodger Specific Mark II Drive Core Card. With this booster you can now take games of Firefly: The Game up to five players[/q]
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I will be attending BGG Spring and am now planning to have a seller table. :arrowE: I accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. I also accept Venmo or Cash. :arrowE: I use [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Condition_of_a_game]this article[/url] for determining the condition of the items I have for sale.
